# createWorkletRuntime

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/createWorkletRuntime

# createWorkletRuntime

`createWorkletRuntime` lets you create a new JS runtime which can be used to run [worklet functions](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#worklet-functions) possibly on different threads than [JS](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model) or [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model). Use this function if you need to integrate with Worklet Runtimes in C++.

The return value represents the runtime. You can pass it to the C++ side using JSI (JavaScript Interface) for further operations.

## Reference

### Usage in JavaScript

The initializer runs in the new runtime **on the creating thread**, before `createWorkletRuntime` returns. It sets a global variable that the scheduled task later reads on the worker's own thread. Compare the thread IDs in the console: the initializer and creator match, while the scheduled task has a different ID.

```js
import {
  createWorkletRuntime,
  getCurrentThreadId,
  scheduleOnRuntime,
} from 'react-native-worklets';

function initialize() {
  'worklet';
  (globalThis.message = 'Ready');
  console.log('Initializer thread:', getCurrentThreadId());
}

function runTask() {
  'worklet';
  console.log(globalThis.message); // Ready
  console.log('Worker thread:', getCurrentThreadId());
}

const worker = createWorkletRuntime({
  name: 'background',
  initializer: initialize,
});
console.log('Creator thread:', getCurrentThreadId());
scheduleOnRuntime(worker, runTask);
```

### Usage in C++

```cpp
#include <worklets/WorkletRuntime/WorkletRuntime.h>

void scheduleNativeWork(
    facebook::jsi::Runtime &rnRuntime,
    const facebook::jsi::Value &runtimeValue) {
  auto worker = worklets::extractWorkletRuntime(rnRuntime, runtimeValue);

  worker->schedule([](facebook::jsi::Runtime &workerRuntime) {
    workerRuntime.global().setProperty(workerRuntime, "nativeWorkFinished", true);
  });
}
```

`rnRuntime` owns the incoming `runtimeValue`. The scheduled callback receives the worker's JSI runtime and runs on its queue with the runtime lock held. Keep the default queue and locking enabled for this example, and retain the Worker Runtime while its work is pending.

Use `worker->runSync(...)` for a short synchronous operation on the calling thread.

Type definitions

```typescript
type WorkletRuntime = {
  __hostObjectWorkletRuntime: never;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly runtimeId: number;
};

type WorkletRuntimeConfig = {
  name?: string;
  initializer?: () => void;
  animationQueuePollingRate?: number;
  enableNetworking?: boolean;
  abortable?: boolean;
  queue?: 'default' | object | null;
} & (
  | { enableEventLoop?: boolean; enableLocking?: true }
  | { enableEventLoop?: false; enableLocking: false }
);

function createWorkletRuntime(
  config?: WorkletRuntimeConfig
): WorkletRuntime;
```

### Arguments

#### `config`

Runtime configuration object.

##### `name`

A name of the runtime used in debugging. Defaults to `'anonymous'`.

##### `initializer`

An optional worklet function that will be run synchronously on the same thread immediately after the runtime is created. It can be used to inject some global variables or functions into the runtime.

##### `animationQueuePollingRate`

Time interval in milliseconds between polling of frame callbacks scheduled by `requestAnimationFrame`. Defaults to `16`.

##### `enableEventLoop`

Determines whether to enable the default event loop. Defaults to `true`. Always disabled on runtimes with `enableLocking: false`.
When enabled, the runtime provides `setTimeout`, `setImmediate`, `setInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `queueMicrotask`, `clearTimeout`, `clearInterval`, `clearImmediate`, and `cancelAnimationFrame`.

##### `enableNetworking`

Determines whether the [networking API](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/bundleMode/usage#running-network-requests-in-worklets) - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest` and their supporting globals - is installed on the Runtime. Defaults to `true`.

##### `abortable`

Determines whether the Runtime can be stopped with [abortWorkletRuntime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/abortWorkletRuntime). With a custom queue, the Runtime's pending jobs are dropped only if the queue implements `AsyncQueue::stop`. Defaults to `false`.

##### `enableLocking`

Determines whether access to the underlying JS runtime is synchronized with a mutex around every JSI operation. If not specified, it defaults to `true`.
Can be disabled only together with the Event Loop.

Runtime without locking doesn't receive HMR updates and new Custom Serializable registrations.

Disable only when you can guarantee thread safety of all access to the runtime.

##### `queue`

Controls the queue used for scheduling worklet functions on this runtime. Defaults to `'default'`.

* `'default'`: use the built-in queue implementation.
* An object implementing the C++ `AsyncQueue` interface from `<worklets/RunLoop/AsyncQueue.h>`: use the provided custom queue.
* `null`: do not attach any queue to the Runtime. Keep in mind that this will effectively disable all asynchronous features like Promises, `setTimeout` etc. Use it if you're going to implement the event-loop for the Runtime yourself.

### Returns

`createWorkletRuntime` returns a JavaScript object backed by a C++ `worklets::WorkletRuntime`, which derives from `jsi::HostObject`.

## Remarks

* Worklet runtimes come with `performance.now` and `console.*` methods installed out-of-the-box. Other APIs are not available and need to be injected into the runtime or captured via worklet closure.

* In development mode, all unhandled errors thrown in the runtime (except for those thrown in `initializer`) will be caught and thus logged to the console and displayed in a LogBox.

## Platform compatibility

| Native    | Web           |
| --------- | ------------- |
| Supported | Not supported |

---

# executeOnUIRuntimeSync

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/executeOnUIRuntimeSync

Deprecated API.

# executeOnUIRuntimeSync

`executeOnUIRuntimeSync` lets you run a [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) function synchronously on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model).

## Reference

```jsx
import { executeOnUIRuntimeSync } from 'react-native-worklets';

// RN Runtime, JS thread

const result: number = executeOnUIRuntimeSync((): number => {
  return 1;
})();

console.log(result); // 1
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function executeOnUIRuntimeSync<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  worklet: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue
): (...args: Args) => ReturnValue;
```

### Arguments

#### worklet

A reference to a function you want to execute on the UI Runtime on the current thread. Arguments to your function have to be passed to the function returned from `executeOnUIRuntimeSync` i.e. `executeOnUIRuntimeSync(setValue)(10);`.

### Returns

`executeOnUIRuntimeSync` returns the return value of the worklet function.

> INFO
>
> Don't forget to call the function returned from `executeOnUIRuntimeSync`.

## Remarks

* It's a common mistake to execute function inside of `executeOnUIRuntimeSync` like this: ~~`executeOnUIRuntimeSync(myWorklet(10))()`~~. Here, the correct usage would be `executeOnUIRuntimeSync(myWorklet)(10)`.

* The callback passed as the argument is automatically [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) and ready to be run on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model).

* Make sure not to execute `executeOnUIRuntimeSync` on the UI thread as this will result in an error.

---

# runOnJS

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnJS

Deprecated API.

# runOnJS

`runOnJS` lets you asynchronously run non-[workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) functions that couldn't otherwise run on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model). This applies to most external libraries as they don't have their functions marked with `"worklet";` directive.

`runOnJS` is usually used to update React state either on animation finish or conditionally within a gesture.

## Reference

```javascript
import { runOnJS } from 'react-native-worklets';

function App() {
  // While on the UI thread
  runOnJS(navigation.goBack)();
}
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnJS<A extends any[], R>(
  fn: (...args: A) => R
): (...args: Parameters<typeof fn>) => void;
```

### Arguments

#### fn

A reference to a function you want to execute on the [JavaScript thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model) from the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model). Arguments to your function have to be passed to the function returned from `runOnJS` i.e. `runOnJS(setValue)(10);`.

### Returns

`runOnJS` returns a function that accepts arguments for the function passed as the first argument. This function can be safely executed on the UI thread.

> INFO
>
> Don't forget to call the function returned from `runOnJS`.

## Example

## Remarks

* Functions passed to `runOnJS` must be defined in the [JavaScript thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model) scope, i.e. in the component body or the global scope. The code below won't work because `myFunction` is defined in the `withTiming` callback, which is only executed in the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model):

```jsx
withTiming(0, {}, () => {
  // myFunction is defined on the UI thread 🚨
  const myFunction = () => {
    // ...
  };
  runOnJS(myFunction)(); // 💥
});
```

* It's a common mistake to execute function inside of runOnJS like this: ~~`runOnJS(setValue(10))()`~~. Here, the correct usage would be `runOnJS(setValue)(10)`.

* It's safe to run functions via `runOnJS` on the [JavaScript thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model). In this case the function is scheduled with `queueMicrotask` and runs asynchronously.

---

# runOnRNSync

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRNSync

# runOnRNSync

`runOnRNSync` lets you run a function synchronously on the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime) from any runtime and get its return value. The calling thread waits until the JavaScript thread finishes running the function.

## Reference

```javascript
import { runOnRNSync, scheduleOnUI } from 'react-native-worklets';

const getUserName = (): string => store.user.name;

scheduleOnUI(() => {
  'worklet';
  const name = runOnRNSync(getUserName);
  console.log(name);
});
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnRNSync<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  fun: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue,
  ...args: Args
): ReturnValue;
```

### Arguments

#### fun

A function you want to execute on the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime). It can be a function defined on the RN Runtime, a [worklet](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#worklet-functions) or a host function. The same functions as in [`scheduleOnRN`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/scheduleOnRN#what-functions-can-be-passed-to-scheduleonrn) are accepted.

#### args

Arguments to pass to the function. They must be convertible to a [Serializable](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/memory/serializable).

### Returns

`runOnRNSync` returns the return value of the function passed as the first argument. It can only return values that can be converted to a [Serializable](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/memory/serializable).

## Remarks

* When called on the RN Runtime, `runOnRNSync` calls the function directly.
* On the UI Runtime and Worker Runtimes, `runOnRNSync` works only with the [Bundle Mode](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/bundleMode).
* An error thrown by the function is rethrown on the calling runtime with the same message. In development builds its stack holds the RN Runtime frames, labeled `[RN]`, followed by the stack of the `runOnRNSync` call.
* The calling thread is blocked while the JavaScript thread runs the function. Don't call `runOnRNSync` in code that runs every frame.
* `runOnRNSync` deadlocks if the JavaScript thread is waiting for the calling runtime at the same time. For example, a worklet on the UI Runtime must not call `runOnRNSync` while the RN Runtime waits in [`runOnUISync`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUISync) for the UI Runtime. Calling `runOnRNSync` from inside `runOnUISync` is safe, because that worklet already runs on the JavaScript thread.

## Call table

| Mode             | RN Runtime | UI Runtime    | Worker Runtime |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| Bundle Mode      | Supported  | Supported     | Supported      |
| Legacy Eval Mode | Supported  | Not supported | Not supported  |

## Platform compatibility

| Native    | Web       |
| --------- | --------- |
| Supported | Supported |

---

# runOnRuntime

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRuntime

Deprecated API.

# runOnRuntime

`runOnRuntime` lets you asynchronously run [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) functions on a separate worklet runtime on a separate thread.

## Reference

```javascript
import { createWorkletRuntime, runOnRuntime } from 'react-native-worklets';

const workletRuntime = createWorkletRuntime({ name: 'background' });

function App() {
  // E.g. in event handler or in an effect
  // highlight-next-line
  runOnRuntime(workletRuntime, (greeting) => {
    console.log(`${greeting} from a separate thread`);
    // highlight-next-line
  })('Howdy');

  // ...
}
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnRuntime<A extends any[], R>(
  workletRuntime: WorkletRuntime,
  fn: (...args: A) => R
): (...args: Parameters<typeof fn>) => void;
```

### Arguments

#### workletRuntime

A reference to worklet runtime created with [`createWorkletRuntime`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/createWorkletRuntime).

#### fn

A reference to a function you want to execute on the worklet runtime passed as `workletRuntime`. Arguments to your function have to be passed to the function returned from `runOnRuntime` i.e. `runOnRuntime(workletRuntime, myWorklet)(10);`.

### Returns

`runOnRuntime` returns a function that accepts arguments for the function passed as the first argument.

> INFO
>
> Don't forget to call the function returned from `runOnRuntime`.

## Remarks

* It's a common mistake to execute function inside of `runOnRuntime` like this: ~~`runOnRuntime(myWorklet(10))()`~~. Here, the correct usage would be `runOnRuntime(myWorklet)(10)`.

* The callback passed as the argument will not be [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) automatically. You need to add `'worklet';` directive manually to allow the function to be run on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model).

* You may call `runOnRuntime` on any runtime, including the RN runtime, UI runtime and other worklet runtimes.

* The function passed to `runOnRuntime` will be added to an execution queue on a separate thread and executed asynchronously on the specified worklet runtime. The functions will be executed in the order they were added to the queue.

---

# runOnRuntimeAsync

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRuntimeAsync

# runOnRuntimeAsync

`runOnRuntimeAsync` lets you asynchronously run [worklet functions](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#worklet-functions) on a [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime).
It returns a Promise of the worklet function's return value. The Promise is resolved asynchronously, not immediately after the callback execution.

## Reference

```js
import { createWorkletRuntime, runOnRuntimeAsync } from 'react-native-worklets';

function sum(numbers) {
  'worklet';
  return numbers.reduce((total, n) => total + n, 0);
}

const workletRuntime = createWorkletRuntime({ name: 'background' });
const data = [1, 2, 3, 4];
const pending = runOnRuntimeAsync(workletRuntime, sum, data);
console.log('The RN Runtime continues while the worker computes');
const result = await pending;
console.log('Computation result:', result); // 10
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnRuntimeAsync<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  workletRuntime: WorkletRuntime,
  worklet: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue,
  ...args: Args
): Promise<ReturnValue>;
```

## Arguments

### workletRuntime

The worklet runtime to run the worklet function on. Created with [`createWorkletRuntime`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/createWorkletRuntime).

### worklet

A reference to a function you want to execute on the [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime). Arguments to your function have to be passed after the worklet function i.e. `runOnRuntimeAsync(workletRuntime, setValue, 10);`.

### args

Arguments to the function you want to execute on the [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime).

## Remarks

* It's a common mistake to execute function inside of `runOnRuntimeAsync` like this: ~~`runOnRuntimeAsync(workletRuntime, myWorklet(10))`~~. Here, the correct usage would be `runOnRuntimeAsync(workletRuntime, myWorklet, 10)`.

* The callback passed as the argument is automatically [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) and ready to be run on the [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime).

* Errors thrown in the worklet function will cause the Promise to reject with that error.

## Call table

| Mode             | RN Runtime | UI Runtime    | Worker Runtime |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| Bundle Mode      | Supported  | Supported     | Supported      |
| Legacy Eval Mode | Supported  | Not supported | Not supported  |

## Platform compatibility

| Native    | Web           |
| --------- | ------------- |
| Supported | Not supported |

---

# runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId

# runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId

`runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId` is a variant of [runOnRuntimeAsync](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRuntimeAsync) where you use the runtime's id instead of the runtime object. It's useful when you don't have access to the runtime object, but you know its id.

## Reference

```js
import {
  createWorkletRuntime,
  runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId,
} from 'react-native-worklets';

function sum(numbers) {
  'worklet';
  return numbers.reduce((total, n) => total + n, 0);
}

const workletRuntime = createWorkletRuntime({ name: 'background' });
const data = [1, 2, 3, 4];
const pending = runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId(
  workletRuntime.runtimeId,
  sum,
  data
);
console.log('The RN Runtime continues while the worker computes');
const result = await pending;
console.log('Computation result:', result); // 10
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  runtimeId: number,
  worklet: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue,
  ...args: Args
): Promise<ReturnValue>;
```

## Arguments

### runtimeId

The id of the [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime) to run the worklet function on. You can get the id from the runtime object by accessing its `runtimeId` property.

### worklet

A reference to a function you want to execute on the [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime).

### args

Arguments to the function you want to execute on the [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime).

## Remarks

* `runOnRuntimeAsyncWithId` can target the UI Runtime by passing [UIRuntimeId](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/uiRuntimeId) as the runtime id.

* Errors thrown in the worklet function will cause the Promise to reject with that error.

## Call table

| Mode             | RN Runtime | UI Runtime    | Worker Runtime |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| Bundle Mode      | Supported  | Supported     | Supported      |
| Legacy Eval Mode | Supported  | Not supported | Not supported  |

## Platform compatibility

| Native    | Web           |
| --------- | ------------- |
| Supported | Not supported |

# runOnRuntimeSync

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRuntimeSync

# runOnRuntimeSync

`runOnRuntimeSync` lets you run a [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) function synchronously on a [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime). It's blocking - meaning that it can preempt the runtime from a thread that's currently executing it.

## Reference

```js
import { createWorkletRuntime, runOnRuntimeSync } from 'react-native-worklets';

function compute() {
  'worklet';
  return 2 + 2;
}

const workletRuntime = createWorkletRuntime({ name: 'background' });
// Blocks the calling thread until the worklet finishes.
const result = runOnRuntimeSync(workletRuntime, compute);
console.log(result); // 4
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnRuntimeSync<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  workletRuntime: WorkletRuntime,
  worklet: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue,
  ...args: Args
): ReturnValue;
```

## Arguments

### workletRuntime

The worklet runtime to run the worklet function on.

### worklet

A reference to a function you want to execute on the [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime).

### args

Arguments to the function you want to execute on the [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime).

## Call table

| Mode             | RN Runtime | UI Runtime    | Worker Runtime |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| Bundle Mode      | Supported  | Supported     | Supported      |
| Legacy Eval Mode | Supported  | Not supported | Not supported  |

## Platform compatibility

| Native    | Web           |
| --------- | ------------- |
| Supported | Not supported |

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRuntimeSyncWithId

# runOnRuntimeSyncWithId

`runOnRuntimeSyncWithId` is a variant of [runOnRuntimeSync](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnRuntimeSync) where you use the runtime's id instead of the runtime object. It's useful when you don't have access to the runtime object, but you know its id.

### runtimeId

# runOnUI

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUI

Deprecated API.

# runOnUI

`runOnUI` lets you asynchronously run [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) functions on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model).

Most commonly used either with an `useEffect` to start an animation on component mount/unmount or with [`measure`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-reanimated/docs/advanced/measure) and [`scrollTo`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-reanimated/docs/scroll/scrollTo) functions which have implementations only on the UI thread.

## Reference

```javascript
import { runOnUI } from 'react-native-worklets';

function App() {
  // E.g. in event handler or in an effect
  // highlight-next-line
  runOnUI((greeting) => {
    console.log(`${greeting} from the UI thread`);
    // highlight-next-line
  })('Howdy');

  // ...
}
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnUI<A extends any[], R>(
  fn: (...args: A) => R
): (...args: Parameters<typeof fn>) => void;
```

### Arguments

#### fn

A reference to a function you want to execute on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model) from the [JavaScript thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model). Arguments to your function have to be passed to the function returned from `runOnUI` i.e. `runOnUI(myWorklet)(10);`.

### Returns

`runOnUI` returns a function that accepts arguments for the function passed as the first argument.

> INFO
>
> Don't forget to call the function returned from `runOnUI`.

## Example

## Remarks

* When implementing your animations you should first reach for more general solutions such as [`useDerivedValue`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-reanimated/docs/core/useDerivedValue), [`useAnimatedReaction`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-reanimated/docs/advanced/useAnimatedReaction) or running code in gesture callbacks and only use `runOnUI` after you've tried other methods.

* It's a common mistake to execute function inside of runOnUI like this: ~~`runOnUI(myWorklet(10))()`~~. Here, the correct usage would be `runOnUI(myWorklet)(10)`.

* The callback passed as the argument is automatically [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) and ready to be run on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model).

* Make sure not to execute `runOnUI` on the UI thread as this will result in an error.

* In browsers there's no separate UI thread available. Because of that, on the Web, `runOnUI` behaves similarly to `requestAnimationFrame`. It creates a function that, when called, will be scheduled to run with given arguments on next animation frame.

---

# runOnUIAsync

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUIAsync

# runOnUIAsync

`runOnUIAsync` lets you asynchronously run [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) functions on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model).
It returns a Promise of the worklet function's return value. The Promise is resolved asynchronously, not immediately after the callback execution.

To compare it with [`scheduleOnUI`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/scheduleOnUI) and [`runOnUISync`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUISync), see [Running worklet functions on the UI runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/guides/running-on-the-ui-runtime).

## Reference

```js
import { runOnUIAsync } from 'react-native-worklets';

function compute() {
  'worklet';
  return 1;
}

const pending = runOnUIAsync(compute);
console.log('The RN Runtime continues while the result is pending');
const result = await pending;
console.log(result); // 1
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnUIAsync<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  worklet: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue,
  ...args: Args
): Promise<ReturnValue>;
```

### Arguments

#### worklet

A reference to a function you want to execute on the UI thread. Arguments to your function have to be passed after the function i.e. `runOnUIAsync(setValue, 10);`.

## Remarks

* It's a common mistake to execute function inside of `runOnUIAsync` like this: ~~`runOnUIAsync(myWorklet(10))`~~. Here, the correct usage would be `runOnUIAsync(myWorklet, 10)`.

* The callback passed as the argument is automatically [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) and ready to be run on the [UI thread](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#the-react-native-model).

## Call table

| Mode             | RN Runtime | UI Runtime    | Worker Runtime |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| Bundle Mode      | Supported  | Supported     | Supported      |
| Legacy Eval Mode | Supported  | Not supported | Not supported  |

## Platform compatibility

| Native    | Web       |
| --------- | --------- |
| Supported | Supported |

# runOnUISync

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUISync

# runOnUISync

`runOnUISync` lets you run a [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) function synchronously on the [UI Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#ui-runtime).

To compare it with [`scheduleOnUI`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/scheduleOnUI) and [`runOnUIAsync`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUIAsync), see [Running worklet functions on the UI runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/guides/running-on-the-ui-runtime).

## Reference

```js
import { runOnUISync } from 'react-native-worklets';

function myFunction(num) {
  'worklet';
  return num + 1;
}

const result = runOnUISync(myFunction, 0);
console.log(result); // 1
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function runOnUISync<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  worklet: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue,
  ...args: Args
): ReturnValue;
```

### Arguments

#### worklet

A function you want to execute on the [UI Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#ui-runtime).

#### args

Arguments to pass to the function.

### Returns

`runOnUISync` returns the return value of the function passed as the first argument. It can only return values that can be converted to a [Serializable](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/memory/serializable).

## Remarks

* The callback passed as the argument is automatically [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) and ready to be run on the [UI Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#ui-runtime).

## Call table

| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------- |

# scheduleOnRN

Source: https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/scheduleOnRN

# scheduleOnRN

`scheduleOnRN` lets you schedule a function to be executed on the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime) from any [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime).

To learn more about the different runtime kinds, check [Runtime Kinds](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds).

`scheduleOnRN` is commonly used to update React state from [UI Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#ui-runtime), e.g. when animation finishes or conditionally within a gesture.

## Reference

```js
import { scheduleOnRN, scheduleOnUI } from 'react-native-worklets';

function onResult(result) {
  console.log('Result on the RN Runtime:', result);
}

function compute() {
  'worklet';
  const result = 2 + 2;
  scheduleOnRN(onResult, result);
}

scheduleOnUI(compute);
```

Type definitions

```typescript
function scheduleOnRN<Args extends unknown[], ReturnValue>(
  fun:
    | ((...args: Args) => ReturnValue)
    | RemoteFunction<Args, ReturnValue>
    | WorkletFunction<Args, ReturnValue>,
  ...args: Args
): void;
```

### Arguments

#### fn

A reference to a function you want to execute on the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime).

#### args

Arguments to the function you want to execute on the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime).

## Example

## Remarks

### What functions can be passed to `scheduleOnRN`?

Functions passed to `scheduleOnRN` must be defined on the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime) scope, i.e. in the component body or the global scope. The code below won't work because `myFunction` is defined in the `scheduleOnUI` callback, which is only executed on the [UI Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#ui-runtime).

```jsx
import { scheduleOnRN, scheduleOnUI } from 'react-native-worklets';

function App() {
  //... component code

  scheduleOnUI(() => {
    // callback is defined on the UI Runtime 🚨
    // highlight-next-line
    scheduleOnRN(() => {}); // 💥
  });

  //... other component code
}
```

To fix it, you have to move the function definition to the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime) scope:

```jsx
import { scheduleOnRN, scheduleOnUI } from 'react-native-worklets';

function App() {
  //... component code

  // myFunction is defined on the RN Runtime ✅
  // highlight-next-line
  const myFunction = () => {};

  scheduleOnUI(() => {
    scheduleOnRN(myFunction); // 🥳
  });

  //... other component code
}
```

## Implementation Details

* Scheduling function from the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime) (we are already on RN Runtime) simply
  uses `queueMicrotask`.
* When functions need to be scheduled from a [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime), they rely on React Native's scheduling model to forward the function call to the [RN Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#rn-runtime).

## Call table

| Mode             | RN Runtime | UI Runtime | Worker Runtime |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ---------- | -------------- |
| Bundle Mode      | Supported  | Supported  | Supported      |
| Legacy Eval Mode | Supported  | Supported  | Supported      |

## Platform compatibility

| Native    | Web       |
| --------- | --------- |
| Supported | Supported |

# scheduleOnRuntime

`scheduleOnRuntime` lets you schedule a [worklet function](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/tutorials/concurrency-model#worklet-functions) to be executed on a [Worker Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worker-runtime).

# scheduleOnRuntimeWithId

`scheduleOnRuntimeWithId` is a variant of [scheduleOnRuntime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/scheduleOnRuntime) where you use the runtime's id instead of the runtime object. It's useful when you don't have access to the runtime object, but you know its id.

## Reference

```js
import {
  createWorkletRuntime,
  scheduleOnRuntimeWithId,
} from 'react-native-worklets';

function greet(greeting) {
  'worklet';
  console.log(`${greeting} from the background Worklet Runtime`);
}

const workletRuntime = createWorkletRuntime({ name: 'background' });
scheduleOnRuntimeWithId(workletRuntime.runtimeId, greet, 'Hello');
console.log('The RN Runtime continues');
```

Type definitions

```typescript

  runtimeId: number,
  worklet: (...args: Args) => ReturnValue,
  ...args: Args
): void;
```

## Arguments

### runtimeId

The id of the [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime) to schedule the worklet function on. You can get the id from the runtime object by accessing its `runtimeId` property.

### worklet

A reference to a function you want to execute on the [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime).

### args

Arguments to the function you want to execute on the [Worklet Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#worklet-runtime).

## Remarks

* The worklet function is scheduled on the Worker Runtime's [Async
  Queue](https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-reanimated/blob/main/packages/react-native-worklets/Common/cpp/worklets/RunLoop/AsyncQueue.h)
* You can target the UI Runtime by passing [UIRuntimeId](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/uiRuntimeId) as the runtime id.

# scheduleOnUI

`scheduleOnUI` lets you schedule a function to be executed on the [UI Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#ui-runtime). The callback executes asynchronously and doesn't return a value.

To compare it with [`runOnUIAsync`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUIAsync) and [`runOnUISync`](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/threading/runOnUISync), see [Running worklet functions on the UI runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/guides/running-on-the-ui-runtime).

```js
import { scheduleOnUI } from 'react-native-worklets';

  'worklet';
  console.log('Hello from the UI Runtime!');
}

scheduleOnUI(myFunction);
console.log('The RN Runtime continues');
```

## Remarks

* The callback passed as the argument is automatically [workletized](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/worklets-plugin/about#autoworkletization) and ready to be run on the [UI Runtime](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-worklets/docs/unreleased/concepts/runtimeKinds#ui-runtime).
